authority: owner finding 2026-08-22, verified against the graded artifacts before acceptance
the_finding_owner_wording: home teams went 14-1. V2 was 10-1 on its home picks but 0-4 on away picks, so the 10-5 headline overstates how discriminating the card was.

verification.note: BOTH cohorts went 0-for on every away pick. Neither model got a single away call right.

the_sharper_version_of_the_caveat.conclusion: A trivial always-pick-home heuristic BEAT v2 outright on this slate, by four games. The 10-5 record therefore does not merely overstate discrimination — on this night it was worse than the crudest possible base-rate strategy. The Brier still beats a flat 50% (.23062 vs .25000), so the probabilities carried some information, but the WIN-LOSS headline is actively misleading and must never be quoted alone.

what_this_does_and_does_not_do_to_the_st.does_not_invalidate: the v1-vs-v2 comparison is still internally valid: both cohorts faced the same 14-1 home slate, so the base rate is common to both and cannot explain the DIFFERENCE between them.
what_this_does_and_does_not_do_to_the_st.does_qualify: but the v2 gain came from 4 flips (STL@PHI, TB@BAL, MIN@SD gained; LAA@TEX lost), and three of the four gains were flips TOWARD the home side on a night when home teams went 14-1. On a neutral or away-heavy slate the same starter information could have flipped those the other way. n=15, 4 flips: the effect is not established.
what_this_does_and_does_not_do_to_the_st.revised_claim: v2 outperformed v1 on this slate. That is descriptive. It is NOT a measured starter effect, both because the simulation coupling is not separated in the registered deltas and because the flips align with an extreme base rate.

owner_numbers_reproduced_exactly: flips: PHI, BAL, SD gained; LAA lost
